I have it on my phone. It blocks mostly everything on its own right now in beta. I think a major part of the plan will be its "replacement" ads will be simple, non animated images, designed to load fast and not eat your bandwidth.

The beta of this has been pretty good. Pages do load super fast, and I havent had a single "pop over" add that covers my whole mobile page. This includes pages that like to bug you about viewing them in their app which you don't want every time you go there (cough pinterest cough cough). Currently, web site banner adds are being replaced by a bar that says "this add will be replaced by something better soon" with the brave logo.

As a result, I have noticed a marked decrease in my data usage. Fuck paying for bandwidth just to have it eaten by animated adverts and pop overs.

You know... theoretically it's not a terrible idea.

People increasingly use adblock because there are literally no downsides to it. It's nothing but positives. Pages load faster, you won't get slammed with obnoxious video ads that begin blasting audio, and then there is the ever present risk of malware sneaking in. And this has the trickle down effect of starving web publishers of ad revenue.

So you need to give users some incentive, no matter how small, to not block ads. Begging sort of, kind of works with some communities. But I don't think anybody wants eBegging to be the predominant business model on the web. And subscription models mostly just slowly choke out your growth.

Soooo we'll see. Somehow I don't think this will catch on, or change the web. But you never know.
